theme: The Brothers' War: Urza, Mishra, and the Ruin of Argoth
status: FINISHED PROPOSAL — not approved/locked by Cory
narrator_note: Ramos is both a historically relevant Brothers' War dragon engine and a WUBRG-capable Commander. He fought under Mishra and was later reprogrammed by Urza, eventually saving refugees; the latter details are attested in later Mercadia storytelling rather than a literal Ramos printed flavor text.
canon_caveats: Ramos was a Mishra dragon engine reprogrammed by Urza and is a thematic eyewitness narrator; his printed card has no flavor text and later Mercadia narratives supply his detailed story.

Urza, Planeswalker; Mishra, Lost to Phyrexia; and Titania, Gaea Incarnate are meld BACK FACES and cannot be added as separate cards. Both front physical cards for Urza/Mishra and Titania's land are included.
The Brothers' War (BRC) and The Antiquities War (DOM) are retrospective sagas, not eyewitness records from the exact ending of the war.
Glacial Chasm and snow-covered basic lands evoke the Ice Age aftermath but are not claims about a precise Sylex crater location.
The story spans decades: group order is chronological at the act level, while some cards within an act depict parallel action.
Ramos's WUBRG color identity permits including Urza, Mishra, the Third Path, and Argoth; no off-color or duplicate nonbasic cards are intentionally allowed.
Gix is a praetor manipulating the brothers, but the broader Phyrexian portal later reopened millennia afterward. A modern-return printing such as Portal to Phyrexia is intentionally omitted.

beats.title: I. Two boys, one discovery: Tocasia, the Powerstones, and the broken bond

cards.name: Tocasia's Welcome
cards.why: Tocasia receives the orphaned brothers, creating the human beginning of the tragedy.

cards.name: Tocasia, Dig Site Mentor
cards.why: The archeologist and adoptive teacher who guides Urza and Mishra to the Thran ruins.

cards.name: Loran, Disciple of History
cards.why: Tocasia's devoted student and a future steward of the Sylex story; importantly, not a third brother.

cards.name: Urza, Powerstone Prodigy
cards.why: Urza as the curious young scholar before power and bitterness consume his life.

cards.name: Mishra, Excavation Prodigy
cards.why: Mishra as the skilled young desert explorer, contrasted by the original card's flavor.

cards.name: Ornithopter
cards.why: An early mechanical experiment; Antiquities printing explicitly treats it as Urza's youthful artifice.

cards.name: Mightstone
cards.why: The stone Urza discovers in the Hall of Tagsin, according to the Antiquities flavor text.

cards.name: Weakstone
cards.why: The stone Mishra discovers in the same underground chamber, according to the Antiquities flavor text.

cards.name: Splitting the Powerstone
cards.why: The original Brothers' War card records the breakup of the stone and the brothers' relationship.

cards.name: Sibling Rivalry
cards.why: An explicit title for their competition before it becomes a war among nations.

cards.name: Brotherhood's End
cards.why: Tocasia's death as the brothers fight, the decisive end of their childhood together.

beats.title: II. Rival empires: Kroog, Mak Fawa, the engineers and the war machines

cards.name: Urza, Prince of Kroog
cards.why: Urza enters the court of Yotia through Kayla and becomes the formidable artificer of Kroog.

cards.name: Queen Kayla bin-Kroog
cards.why: Kayla, Urza's wife and an eyewitness whose history preserves much of this era.

cards.name: Harbin, Vanguard Aviator
cards.why: The royal son and aviator who wants to fight for Yotia and win his father's respect.

cards.name: Tawnos, the Toymaker
cards.why: Urza's inventive apprentice represents the human ingenuity behind the Argivian machines.

cards.name: Drafna, Founder of Lat-Nam
cards.why: The scholar who, with Hurkyl, builds a lasting refuge of learning amid the war.

cards.name: Hurkyl, Master Wizard
cards.why: A Third Path wizard and counterweight to the brothers' destructive artifact obsession.

cards.name: Mishra, Tamer of Mak Fawa
cards.why: Mishra rises as a power among the Fallaji and masters dragon engines.

cards.name: Hajar, Loyal Bodyguard
cards.why: Mishra's devoted companion despite the war's escalating moral cost.

cards.name: Ashnod, Flesh Mechanist
cards.why: Mishra's gifted lieutenant and maker of gruesome war technology.

cards.name: Urza, Chief Artificer
cards.why: A contemporaneous portrait of Urza as a commander of armies of constructs.

cards.name: Mishra, Eminent One
cards.why: An alternate portrait of Mishra's dominion over the artifact armies.

cards.name: Urza's Command
cards.why: An era-specific card commemorating Urza's commands in the war.

cards.name: Mishra's Command
cards.why: Counterpart to Urza's Command; each brother directs a rival technological empire.

beats.title: III. Gix and the machine war: Phyrexian infiltration, Kroog destroyed

cards.name: Gix, Yawgmoth Praetor
cards.why: The Phyrexian praetor secretly manipulates Mishra and the growing conflict.

cards.name: Gate to Phyrexia
cards.why: Original Antiquities artifact and flavor reveal the terrifying world behind the corruption.

cards.name: Disciples of Gix
cards.why: A direct look at the cult that spreads the praetor's influence.

cards.name: Gix's Caress
cards.why: The direct flavor captures Gix delighting in the misery he has cultivated.

cards.name: Gix's Command
cards.why: The praetor's own named command, contrasting his manipulation with the brothers' armies.

cards.name: Mishra, Claimed by Gix
cards.why: The late-war Mishra on the edge of total Phyrexian assimilation; meld front face.

cards.name: Phyrexian Dragon Engine
cards.why: The second actual card required to meld Mishra into Mishra, Lost to Phyrexia.

cards.name: Ashnod's Altar
cards.why: The brutal technological practices associated with Mishra's artificer.

cards.name: Ashnod's Transmogrant
cards.why: Original Antiquities card directly associated with Ashnod's experiments on living bodies.

cards.name: Powerstone Fracture
cards.why: The original BRO printing shows Ashnod using a Powerstone explosion to destroy a war-machine behemoth; this is NOT the childhood splitting of the original stone.

cards.name: Dragon Engine
cards.why: A period Antiquities machine named and illustrated as part of the brothers' industrial warfare.

cards.name: Mishra's War Machine
cards.why: The original era's industrialized destructive force, by Mishra's own name.

cards.name: Mishra's Onslaught
cards.why: Mishra's attack against Urza's defensive positions, explicitly voiced in the original flavor.

cards.name: Mishra's Domination
cards.why: The original printed text describes Mishra binding a dragon engine through the Weakstone.

cards.name: The Fall of Kroog
cards.why: Directly depicts Mishra's destruction of the capital in retaliation for the peace-summit ambush.

beats.title: IV. Witnesses, the Third Path, and the living forest of Argoth

cards.name: Loran of the Third Path
cards.why: A scholar who recognized the Sylex as vital knowledge rather than merely another weapon.

cards.name: The Archimandrite
cards.why: A leading Third Path figure representing the nonaligned tradition endangered by the conflict.

cards.name: Union of the Third Path
cards.why: The independent alliance of scholars trying to respond to the brothers' devastation.

cards.name: Hurkyl's Final Meditation
cards.why: A named decisive moment in Hurkyl's struggle against invading machinery.

cards.name: Loran's Escape
cards.why: The original printing shows Feldon entrusting Loran with the Sylex amid Terisia City's destruction.

cards.name: Ashnod's Intervention
cards.why: Ashnod warns Tawnos that Gix has manipulated both sides.

cards.name: Fateful Handoff
cards.why: Ashnod directs Tawnos to deliver the Sylex to Urza, a decisive handover.

cards.name: Titania, Voice of Gaea
cards.why: Argoth's nature guardian, a victim of the brothers' escalating war.

cards.name: Titania's Song
cards.why: The original Antiquities card represents Titania and Argoth's living resistance.

cards.name: Gwenna, Eyes of Gaea
cards.why: An Argothian character and witness to nature's suffering.

cards.name: Argothian Pixies
cards.why: Original Antiquities flavor situates the small forest folk on Argoth.

cards.name: Argothian Treefolk
cards.why: Original Antiquities flavor preserves the sentient forest caught in the war.

cards.name: Gaea's Gift
cards.why: The Brothers' War-era card literally pits the living forest against Mishra's military force.

cards.name: Titania's Command
cards.why: The nature guardian's own named response to the attack on Argoth.

cards.name: Fallaji Dragon Engine
cards.why: A war machine from Mishra's Fallaji military, representing the invasion of Argoth.

beats.title: V. The last battle, the Sylex Blast, the Ice Age and the history left behind

cards.name: Urza, Lord Protector
cards.why: Urza at the ruinous final battle; meld front face from The Brothers' War.

cards.name: The Mightstone and Weakstone
cards.why: The second actual card needed to meld Urza into Urza, Planeswalker.

cards.name: Golgothian Sylex
cards.why: The original Antiquities printing of the destructive artifact that ends the war.

cards.name: Urza's Sylex
cards.why: A second, war-era illustration of the same weapon, used in Urza's catastrophic decision.

cards.name: Urza's Ruinous Blast
cards.why: Directly memorializes the blast that destroys Argoth and changes Dominaria.

cards.name: Calamity's Wake
cards.why: The original flavor describes snow and sorrow following the blast, with Urza alone.

cards.name: Citanul Druid
cards.why: Antiquities flavor explicitly remembers the Citanul driven mad by Argoth's fall; this is an aftermath card, not a surviving pre-blast army.

cards.name: One with the Multiverse
cards.why: Wizards' Brothers' War design article explicitly identifies this card as Urza becoming a Planeswalker after the final catastrophe.

cards.name: Tawnos, Solemn Survivor
cards.why: Urza's apprentice survives the tragedy and remains a witness to its cost.

cards.name: Kayla's Reconstruction
cards.why: Kayla turns from witnessing destruction to rebuilding the lives left behind.

cards.name: Feldon, Ronom Excavator
cards.why: Feldon survives into the harsh aftermath, keeping the Third Path's history alive.

cards.name: The Brothers' War
cards.why: A Saga card designed to retell the two brothers' long conflict.

cards.name: The Antiquities War
cards.why: A later in-world-history Saga that lets the deck end as an archaeological remembrance.

beats.title: VI. Geography of invention and catastrophe — lands

cards.name: Tocasia's Dig Site
cards.why: Where the brothers study Thran ruins before their relationship is shattered.

cards.name: Caves of Koilos
cards.why: The ancient underground place linked to the Powerstone discoveries; the chosen old printing is a location callback, not a new war scene.

cards.name: Mishra's Factory
cards.why: Original Antiquities land depicting the infrastructure of Mishra's war-making.

cards.name: Mishra's Workshop
cards.why: Original Antiquities land and flavor associated with the machinery of Mishra's side.

cards.name: Mishra's Foundry
cards.why: The Brothers' War land illustrates Mishra's industrial production.

cards.name: Urza's Workshop
cards.why: The wartime workshop; Brothers' War Commander printing explicitly connects it to Urza.

cards.name: Urza's Mine
cards.why: The original Antiquities set's Urza infrastructure; select a specific flavor-text variant.

cards.name: Urza's Power Plant
cards.why: Original Antiquities power infrastructure; select a period-appropriate flavor-text printing.

cards.name: Urza's Tower
cards.why: Original Antiquities fortress of Urza's engineering network.

cards.name: Argoth, Sanctum of Nature
cards.why: Actual meld partner for Titania, Voice of Gaea; the island forest destroyed at the end of the war.

cards.name: Glacial Chasm
cards.why: An Ice Age land illustrating the frozen aftermath, not a documented specific crater of the Sylex Blast.

cards.name: Urza's Saga
cards.why: A later Saga land serving as a retrospective on Urza's long legacy, not an actual battle location.
